The patch builds and tests successfully, but it leaves the closing CTA heading visually hidden in the common animated path and regresses rendering of persisted Fraunces formatting. A lower-severity specificity conflict also disables the intended plate hover transform.

Full review comments:

- [P2] Preserve Fraunces for existing inline marks — /home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/root.tsx:71-73
  Existing manuscripts can persist the previous font option as a `fontFamily` mark containing `"Fraunces", Georgia, serif`; changing the option does not migrate those stored marks. Removing Fraunces from this stylesheet—and from the standalone exporter—therefore makes previously formatted text silently render in Georgia rather than either its selected font or Libre Baskerville. Keep loading Fraunces for compatibility or migrate old marks before removing it.

- [P2] Reveal the closing heading on its observed element — /home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/components/landing/landing-page.tsx:580-583
  With JavaScript, IntersectionObserver, and normal motion enabled, `[data-reveal-ready] .landing-typed-reveal .landing-typed__char` hides these characters, but the observer adds `is-revealed` only to this parent `div`. The matching reveal rule requires `.landing-typed-reveal.is-revealed`, so the visible closing heading remains blank after the section fades in.

- [P3] Let revealed plates retain their hover transform — /home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/global.css:2938-2940
  After the observer adds `is-revealed`, this higher-specificity selector permanently supplies the plate transform and overrides `.landing-plate__figure:hover`. Consequently the newly implemented lift-and-straighten interaction never occurs in the normal JavaScript-enabled landing page, although the hover shadow still changes.
